text:
rachel: Heads up — us-west-2 GPU pools (p4-16k) at sustained 95%+ for the last 20m. Offline drivers + a few hot customers pushed queues to ~2.3k waiting. Observability dashboards show tail latencies spiking for standard tier.

tom: Yikes. Are these mostly long-context jobs or many short chats?

jin: Mixed. 60% short (<128 tokens) but bursty. There's a handful of heavy streaming jobs from partner X causing long KV cache retention.

leo: If it's short token workload dominating, we should be able to shed with admission control instead of cross-region spill immediately. Cross-region adds egress cost and compliance risk.

annie: Agree. Proposal: implement a 3-stage admission policy for saturated pools: 1) soft-probabilistic drop for non-SLA customers, 2) preferential queuing for reserved/dedicated customers using token-budgets, 3) model-fallback to quantized-ggml variants for best-effort traffic.

prasad: Quick numbers — if we probabilistically drop 30% of best-effort requests we can cut queue depth by ~35% and reduce tail P99 by ~20%. But need SLO-safe bounds.

rachel: Sketch of a config I had in mind (pseudo-YAML):
```yaml
admission_control:
  pool: us-west-2-p4
  window_s: 10
  target_util: 0.85
  tiers:
    - name: reserved
      priority: 100
      guaranteed_tokens_per_s: 1200
    - name: standard
      priority: 50
      probabilistic_drop_when_util_gt: 0.88
      drop_rate_formula: "linear(0.0->0.5, 0.88->0.98)"
    - name: best_effort
      priority: 10
      fallback_model: "gptq-6b-8bit"
      fallback_threshold_util: 0.9
```

tom: Love the token budget idea. Can we make the drop_rate formula more conservative for streaming (so users don't get partial streams)? Maybe only apply drop to non-streamed requests.

jin: We can add rule: if request.streaming == true -> use early-reject only (no mid-stream kill). For batch/short ones we can use probabilistic admit.

leo: Also consider locality and residency. For customers with data region constraints, we should avoid cross-region by default and instead throttle them before spillover. Add a per-customer flag: allow_spillover: true/false.

annie: Ops-side: implement two runtime levers: live drop_rate override (for incident runbooks) and auto-scale guardrail that refuses to spin new expensive capacity if cost > threshold. We want to avoid indefinite autoscale during noisy neighbor events.

prasad: Cost note — spilling 20% of traffic to us-east adds ~+$0.12/token egress for some customers on average (ballpark) and doubles networking overhead. For large embedding jobs that's huge. We should prefer local fallback model where possible.

rachel: Agreed. Proposed routing decision tree on saturation: 
1) Is token_budget_remaining(customer) > min_threshold? Yes -> admit locally.
2) Else if customer.allow_spillover && remote_capacity_available && egress_ok -> spill to remote region (respecting residency).
3) Else if fallback_model_exists && quality_degradation_within_margin -> route to fallback locally.
4) Else if customer.tier == reserved -> try preempting best_effort slots in pool.
5) Else -> early-reject with 429 + deterministic backoff header.

tom: Can we encode that 4) preemption logic safely? Preempting requires kill/evict of running KV-holding sessions which can be expensive. Maybe only preempt queued jobs, not running ones.

jin: Good call. Implement preemption only on queued admissions, not on active KV sessions. Active preemption would require checkpointing KV state — not feasible short-term.

leo: For rollout: feature-flag it to a single AZ first, implement metrics: queued_count_by_tier, admitted_by_policy, spillover_count, fallback_count, egress_cost_estimate. Add an alert if fallback_count / admitted_count > 0.2 sustained.

infra-bot: autoscaler: attempted scale_up for us-west-2-pool -> throttled by cost_guardrail (threshold 150k/h).

annie: That's us. If autoscaler is throttled, we need to reduce admission target quickly. Suggest set target_util to 0.75 for affected pools until human override.

prasad: Also add a short-term mitigation: restrict max_concurrent_streams per customer to 6 and enforce per-client window tokens = min( burst_limit, reserved_tokens ). That will blunt the bursts.

rachel: To implement quickly, priority tasks: 1) admission-control runtime + telemetry (tom/jin) 2) config UI for manual overrides (annie) 3) small model-fallback mapping (leo) 4) runbook update + templated 429 responses (prasad).

tom: I'll start a PR with admission server changes and unit tests. Will include the drop formula and an option to target-only non-streaming requests.

jin: I'll wire up dashboards and add the four metrics. Will add an alert: queue_growth_rate > 30% in 5m for 2 consecutive windows.

rachel: Thanks. Schedule a short ops drill tomorrow 10:30 to exercise the flow: simulate 2x short-chat burst and one heavy streaming job.

deploy-bot: deploy request by tom accepted. PR#4821 queued for canary to eng-platform/dev.

annie: I'll prepare the runbook changes and post a TL;DR in #eng-oncall once the feature-flag is ready.

leo: One more thought: add a soft grace period for new customers to avoid onboarding blasts being dropped. New accounts get a 5m warmup token multiplier.

rachel: Good call. We'll iterate after the drill. Thanks team :thumbsup:
